item.title: Count number of jobs in Hudson
item.description:
I wanted to count the number of jobs running on a Hudson server (continuous integration) at work.

 

This javascript counts the number of lines in the table with all jobs:

 

document.getElementById(“projectstatus”).children[0].children.length

 

Or save this as a browser toolbar bookmarklet:

Name: #HudsonJobs
 javascript:(function(e){alert(document.getElementById(“projectstatus”).children[0].children.length);e.preventDefault()})()

This line finds the table with id=“projectstatus”, and counts the TR elements inside of it’s TBODY.

At work it said 445 lines, including the table header.

 

Which means that this hudson server has configured 444 jobs.

item.title: Introducing Tiny JavaScript Number Formatter
item.description:
For a current project, I created a tiny number formatter that inserts thousand delimiters in a string:

10000 to 10,000 etc.

Just add css class=“numberformat currency” to a text field, and it will be formatted automatically.

It is based on the Prototype JavaScript library. You can get it from it’s GitHub repository page. Feel free to add or alter the functionality. Releasing under Creative Commons license.

item.title: Adding Deprecation Warning in JavaScript Console
item.description:
I used this quick trick today to help me clean up and refactor some javascript functions today:

if ("console" in window)
  console.warn('DEPRECATED function call to '+ arguments.callee
  +'\nCalled by:\n'+ arguments.callee.caller );

Which results in a fine deprecation warning in the console:

There is plenty of space for improvement here. Feel free to use or tamper … but please post any alternative suggestions here as a comment.

item.title: Firefox Tip For Framebuster JavaScript
item.description:
I have for long been struggling with an internal legacy application that wraps the content page in a frameset. Very annoying because I have spent some time to reverse engineer a poor-mans API to the application.

Problem: An inline “reverse” framebuster script that makes sure that everything is nicely(?) wrapped in the frameset. As you see it’s included inline in the HTML.

<script Language="Javascript">
  url = "application_url";
  if (parent.frames[0]) {
    if (parent.frames[0].name != 'FrameMain') {
      document.location.replace(url);
    }
  }else{
    document.location.replace(url);
  }
</script>
